title: Edge-to-enterprise sustainment status bridge (LOGSTAT-to-COP automation under DDIL) with plan-coupled fuel/ammunition/parts feasibility forecasting
problem: Battalion-to-division sustainment status (Class I/III/V, maintenance, medical) is still hand-assembled by the S4/SPO from GCSS-Army extracts, voice reports and LOGSTAT spreadsheets and re-keyed into C2 tools, so the commander's sustainment picture lags hours to a day, collapses when disconnected, and operational plans are not automatically checked against fuel/ammunition/parts reality.

user.exact_role: Battalion S4 and BSB support operations officer (SPO) who build and maintain the sustainment COP from LOGSTATs; division G4 planners who produce the sustainment running estimate for each COA
user.echelon: battalion through division, with a theater (TSC/ESC, ASCC G4) variant
organization_examples: 4th Infantry Division and 25th Infantry Division (NGC2 prototype divisions) and I Corps (next)
Division sustainment brigades (DSB) and brigade support battalions (BSB)
21st Theater Sustainment Command / USAREUR-AF (DIU JSDT Gallatin deployment)
USMC combat logistics battalions and MEU/MLR logistics sections (CLC2S users)

current_workflow: Company XO/1SG estimates on-hand fuel, ammunition, water and maintenance status, or pulls GCSS-Army status when a connected terminal is available
Battalion S4 fills the LOGSTAT (unit spreadsheet or DA-format template) and sends it by email, JBC-P free text, chat or FM voice

BSB SPO consolidates LOGSTATs by hand, computes days of supply and builds the brigade sustainment COP (FACT: Army Sustainment Professional Bulletin, summer 2026, describes the S-4 developing and maintaining the sustainment COP by analyzing LOGSTAT data)
Division G4 re-enters the roll-up into CPCE/NGC2 widgets, a sync matrix or PowerPoint; commander briefs from slides
For plan changes, G4 re-runs OPLOG-Planner-style consumption factors in spreadsheets against the new COA; the sustainment estimate is a static slide
On reconnect, requisitions and status captured offline are re-keyed into GCSS-Army; duplicates and stale data are reconciled manually
current_solution: GCSS-Army (SAP ERP, connectivity-dependent) as the system of record; CPCE sustainment widgets / Logistics Reporting Tool (RECALL - not re-verified this session); Palantir Army Vantage/Army Data Platform dashboards at enterprise level; NGC2 prototype data layer with Rune TyrOS as the sustainment application on both NGC2 teams (Rune's five-year $99M IDIQ, June 2026, is a ceiling not revenue); Onebrief for planning (vendor claims sustainment constraints are integrated into COA development); USMC CLC2S (web app being migrated to cloud under LI2S-MC); DIU JSDT prototypes (ASI, Watchtower Labs, Gallatin AI Navigator) at theater/joint level; and, in practice, Excel, PowerPoint and voice.
failure: At the point where unit status (captured on paper, voice or in a spreadsheet at company/battalion) must become structured data in both the ERP and the C2 data layer while the network is degraded: there is no offline-first, doctrinally structured sustainment ledger that syncs deltas in both directions; and at the point where a plan changes: no live link between plan objects (units, tasks, distances, tempo) and consumption/stock models, so feasibility is recomputed by hand. Both failures are acknowledged by the Army (FM 4-0 'predictive logistics' imperative; SBIR PORTAL topic asking for brigade-and-below predictive logistics in contested environments) and are now the object of multiple funded prototypes.

evidence.claim: Army Sustainment Professional Bulletin (summer 2026) still describes the S-4 developing and maintaining the sustainment COP by analyzing LOGSTAT data and communicating requirements to the SPO - i.e., a staff-built, report-driven picture in 2026, even in the modular-brigade concept

why_existing_startups_havent_solved: They are now solving it, but only since 2025-2026 and only at prototype scale: the problem sat unowned for years because it is low-glamour, its inputs (GCSS-Army/LIW readiness and stock data, unit locations) are CUI held by different owners (PEO EIS/CPE ES2 for the ERP, PEO C3T/CPE C2IN for C2, AMC/LDAC for data, CL CFT/CASCOM/G-4 for requirements, USTRANSCOM for movement), and the edge network was too unreliable for a connected SaaS model. What changed is NGC2's open data layer, the CL CFT's Precision Sustainment portfolio, RCCTO/DIU/SBIR money and Army willingness to give commercial software enterprise IDIQs. The result is not an unsolved gap but a crowded, early race (Rune, Gallatin, ASI, Watchtower, C3 AI, NT Concepts, DEFCON AI, Palantir, Onebrief) in which no vendor has yet shown a fielded battalion/brigade capability under DDIL - the residual gap is at the very edge (paper/voice/spreadsheet capture and offline-first sync) and in cross-service and allied logistics.
technical_wedge: A neutral, offline-first 'sustainment data transport' rather than another dashboard: a CRDT/delta-sync ledger with a doctrinal LOGSTAT/OPLOG schema that captures status at company/battalion from the inputs that actually exist (voice, photo of a whiteboard, spreadsheet, JBC-P free text) using on-device speech/vision extraction, auto-computes days of supply and running estimates, and exposes thin adapters (CoT/JSON to NGC2/CPCE, CSV/PDF LOGSTAT, GCSS-Army report exports, Onebrief plan import) plus a stateless 'feasibility-as-a-service' API (COA in, shortfalls by class of supply and time out, with uncertainty). Positioned to sell into Rune/Onebrief/NGC2 integrators as the capture-and-sync layer, or to USMC/allied units that have no Rune equivalent.

mvp.what: Tablet/web app plus sync service: ingest simulated GCSS-Army report exports and company-level inputs (voice/photo/spreadsheet) into a doctrinal LOGSTAT schema; compute days of supply and readiness; peer-to-peer delta sync over intermittent links with conflict resolution; export CoT/JSON to a COP (e.g., TAK) and a formatted LOGSTAT; a plan-feasibility endpoint that consumes a COA JSON (units, tasks, distances, tempo) and applies public OPLOG-style planning factors to output shortfalls over time.
mvp.demonstrable_in_3_6_months: A home-station CPX-style demo with a National Guard/Reserve sustainment unit or a university ROTC/Army Reserve partner using synthetic unit data: show LOGSTAT capture in <2 minutes per company, survival of a 6-hour comms blackout with correct reconciliation on reconnect, live sustainment COP in TAK/ATAK, and a COA feasibility check that updates when the plan changes.
mvp.what_it_must_prove: (1) Capture friction at company level is lower than the current spreadsheet/voice report; (2) the sync model produces no duplicates or stale-data regressions after blackout; (3) the feasibility engine's shortfall predictions match staff estimates on published exercise scenarios; (4) integration into an existing data layer (TAK/CoT first, NGC2/Onebrief later) works without bespoke engineering.

data_requirement.what: Doctrinal planning factors and report formats (FM 4-0, ATP 4-90, OPLOG Planner factors, LOGSTAT templates); realistic unit consumption histories; GCSS-Army/LIW extract formats; plan objects (COA JSON or Onebrief export); ITV/telemetry feeds later.
data_requirement.legally_realistically_obtainable: Public doctrine and planning factors: yes. Real GCSS-Army/LIW/unit LOGSTAT data: CUI, obtainable only through a sponsoring unit, CFT or program office under a data-use agreement and NIST SP 800-171/CMMC L2 handling; theater OPLAN-linked data is classified. A non-US-person founder's access to CUI/export-controlled logistics technical data needs counsel and likely segregation.

entry_vehicle.eligibility_notes: SBIR/STTR requires >50% ownership by US citizens or permanent residents and US-based performance; a German founder who becomes a permanent resident can count toward that, but the Indonesian founder's stake and roles must be structured so the firm meets the ownership test and so no export-controlled logistics technical data or CUI reaches a non-US person without proper authorization (deemed-export and CUI rules) - needs export-control and immigration counsel. DIU OTs and xTech prizes have looser ownership rules but CUI/FOCI questions still arise at prototype stage. Facility/personnel clearances would eventually require a US-person-controlled entity.

incumbent_response.could_anduril_palantir_l3harris_add_it: Yes, easily: Anduril already hosts Rune inside its NGC2 team and could build sustainment widgets on Lattice; Palantir can extend Vantage to edge nodes under the EA; Lockheed's 25th ID data layer can absorb sustainment feeds; Onebrief can add feasibility natively. The Army's stated preference is that sustainment data ride the NGC2 data layer, which the integrators control.
incumbent_response.why_startup_still_wins_or_reject: Mostly reject as a primary bet: the incumbents and 2025-2026 entrants hold the integration slots, the CUI data and the vehicles. A startup wins only in the residual niche the funded players have not shown: (a) the lowest-echelon capture problem (voice/photo/paper/spreadsheet LOGSTAT to structured data on commodity devices) sold as a component to Rune/Onebrief/NGC2 integrators or TAK users; (b) USMC and allied (NATO/Indo-Pacific partner) units that have no Rune equivalent and where GAO has flagged European logistics gaps; (c) a rigorous, open feasibility engine that planning tools call as a service. None of these has demonstrated a large standalone market.

capital_required.assumptions: PoC: two founders plus one contractor, synthetic data conforming to public doctrine formats, TAK/CoT integration, no ATO - within the $250k founder capital. Credible demo: SBIR Phase I/II or DIU OT funded, CUI-capable environment (CMMC L2), IL4/IL5 sandbox, one real integration (GCSS-Army export or NGC2/Onebrief API), participation in an Ivy Sting/PC-C7-type event, 4-8 staff for 12-18 months. Production: ATO, CMMC L2, program-office-approved AESIP/GCSS-Army integration, helpdesk/sustainment, possibly a SIPR instance, 15-30 staff over 2-3 years; task orders on an existing IDIQ are the realistic revenue path, and obligated dollars for this niche are unproven.

Non-US-person founder and CUI/ITAR-adjacent logistics technical data

regulatory_burden.explanation: Generic sustainment software is usually not ITAR-controlled, but maintenance/technical data on specific weapon systems and some military-critical logistics information can be export-controlled; nearly all real inputs (stock levels, readiness, unit locations) are CUI requiring NIST SP 800-171/CMMC Level 2; deployment needs an ATO (IL4/IL5) and, for theater/joint OPLAN-linked use, SIPR and cleared staff. A tactical-echelon product can stay unclassified longer than a joint planning product.
regulatory_burden.non_us_person_founder_note: The Indonesian founder (not assumed a US person) can participate in an unclassified, synthetic-data PoC, but any CUI, export-controlled technical data, SBIR ownership test (>50% US citizens/permanent residents), FOCI review for facility clearance, and personnel-clearance stages require structuring (cap table, roles, access segregation) reviewed by export-control and immigration counsel; this is a constraint to plan for, not a definitive legal judgment.

dual_use_potential.explanation: Offline-first inventory/consumption capture and sync with plan-feasibility forecasting maps to disaster response (FEMA/NGO field logistics), mining/oil-and-gas remote operations, humanitarian supply chains and wildfire incident logistics - all intermittently connected, spreadsheet-driven fields. The doctrinal schema and NGC2 integrations are defense-specific, and no commercial customer was evidenced this session, so the dual-use path is plausible but unproven (HYPOTHESIS).

defensibility.explanation: If it works, the defensible assets are the accredited integrations into GCSS-Army/NGC2/Onebrief, the doctrinal capture workflow adopted by units, historical consumption datasets that improve forecasting, and sponsor relationships - not the algorithms, which incumbents can replicate. All of these are also exactly what Rune, Gallatin and the NGC2 integrators are accumulating first.

why_now: In the last ~3 years: the Contested Logistics CFT formed (Mar 2023) and made predictive logistics a doctrinal imperative (FM 4-0); NGC2 created an open data layer with monthly soldier-touchpoint exercises (Ivy Sting, Ivy Mass, PC-C6) where sustainment data is an intended feed; the Army began paying commercial vendors for exactly this (Rune $99M IDIQ, Gallatin PORTAL, C3 AI RCCTO, DIU JSDT x3); Onebrief's IDIQ and NGC2 role make plan objects programmatically available for the first time; the EBS-C retreat (May 2026) left the ERP side open; and GAO's 2025 restricted reports on Indo-Pacific fuel and European logistics raised oversight pressure. Edge compute, mesh/LEO connectivity and on-device speech/vision models also make offline-first capture feasible on commodity devices.
killer_risk: This is no longer an unowned gap: between June 2025 and September 2026 the Army and DIU selected and funded at least six vendors for edge and theater predictive logistics, including a $99M IDIQ for Rune that is embedded in both NGC2 teams, and the planning incumbent (Onebrief) claims to be absorbing sustainment feasibility. A two-student team with no CUI access, no NGC2 slot and a non-US-person founder would be entering after the Army has already chosen its commercial bets, competing for sub-component crumbs in a low-dollar tactical niche whose obligated spend is still unproven - a classic J (no real startup opportunity for this team) with a B/I residual.

allied_extension: Somewhat more compelling with allies, and possibly the only open lane: GAO-25-106999C (Aug 2025, restricted) found significant gaps in DoD-NATO logistics efforts, USAREUR-AF is the first JSDT deployment target, and most NATO land forces run sustainment on national ERPs plus spreadsheets with no Rune equivalent; a German founder could target Bundeswehr/NATO sustainment (Helsing and Quantum Systems do not cover logistics) and Indo-Pacific partners (Australia/Japan/Philippines) where contested-logistics exercises (Talisman Sabre) are growing. Offsetting factors: allied procurement is slower and more fragmented, FMN/NATO data standards (e.g., MIP/JC3IEDM-derived logistics schemas) add integration burden, and the US-Army-specific doctrinal schema would have to be generalized; no allied solicitation for tactical sustainment-C2 software was verified this session (Public evidence insufficient).
